newsitem.title: USA: PNC Brokerage Corp cuts stock exposure to 60 pct.
newsitem.headline: PNC Brokerage Corp cuts stock exposure to 60 pct.

text.p: PNC Bank Corp's PNC Brokerage Corp says its will cut its exposure to domestic stocks on May 1 "for the first time in many years" by five percent to 60 percent. Bonds were lifted to 40 percent.

Joel Calvo, president and chief executive of PNC Brokerage Corp said in a report that although the U.S. stock market has factored in stronger economic growth, "future rate hikes remain a real threat to the equity market".

He said the market remains vulnerable to news of a rate hike at the Fed's May policy meeting because it has only modest support. The report cited only single-digit forecasts for 1997 corporate earnings of Standard & Poor's 500 companies, high valuations, market volatility and weak performance in secondary stocks.
PNC said it expects the U.S. economy to show even more signs of robust growth than Wall Street is expecting.

"The scenario of faster-then-expected growth, along with the prospects for higher inflation and a boost in short-term rates from the Fed, has tilted the risk-reward balance away from the U.S. equity market," PNC said.
